Don't edit anything, this is a read-only judgment.

THE TWO TICKETS THIS PR CLAIMS TO CLOSE:

**SFCC-736 "pdp/drawer"**: reusable Drawer+Tabs shell only (slide-in panel, backdrop, close button, tab nav header). Explicitly does NOT own tab content. 16 ACs (rendering, backdrop-close, mobile behavior, independent scroll, empty-tabs-still-renders, full keyboard/focus/ARIA/WCAG 2.1 AA).

**SFCC-195 "PDP – Slide Out - Details & Care"**: description literally says "This user story is only for the slide out component and the first Details & Care tab (other tabs covered in separate user stories linked to this)." Content for all other tabs is explicitly out of scope, owned by SFCC-102/266/267/101.

THE PR ALSO INCLUDES, READ THE PLAN DOC FIRST (`.docs/temp/SFCC-736-195-drawer-tabs-plan.md` in the PR branch — it's the author's own decision log, treat it as one input, not ground truth) for full context on each of these before judging:

1. A full rebuild of `ZimmModal`/`useZimmModal` (existing component, unrelated ticket) onto Chakra's `Modal` primitive, justified in the plan doc as "Tim doesn't want two different dialog implementations in the codebase" and done "alongside/before building the new Drawer."
2. A new Tier 2 hook `overrides/app/hooks/use-modal-state.ts`, framed as generic infrastructure other future tickets (SFCC-742, SFCC-801, a not-yet-ticketed mini-cart) will need.
3. `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/productInfo.ts` extended with a large set of additional `c_*` SFCC attribute mappings (colour, colourId, environmentalNotes, fabricComposition, hsCode, sizeFit, styleId, styleNumber, stylingNotes, tabDescription, tabDetails) — per the plan doc, "mapped but not yet wired into any UI," flagged as speculative groundwork for later tabs (SFCC-266, SFCC-102, etc.), not consumed by SFCC-195's own Details & Care content.
4. Real PDP-page wiring (`product-detail/index.tsx`, replacing `InformationAccordion` on the standard product path) — the plan doc calls this "Decision 4 reversed": SFCC-195's own original scope decision was "component-only for this pass... do not touch the PDP page," reversed later once `develop` gained real PDP page overrides from a different branch.

YOUR JOB: for EACH of items 1-4 above, and for the core drawer/tabs/details-care work itself, classify: does it belong to SFCC-736, does it belong to SFCC-195, does it belong to neither (scope creep — flag it, name which ticket if any it should have been), or is it legitimately foundational/shared work that doesn't need its own ticket. Pay special attention to:
- Whether the ZimmModal rebuild is truly necessary for SFCC-736/195, or an unrelated improvement riding along on this branch.
- Whether extending `productInfo.ts` with fields SFCC-195 itself doesn't use is reasonable shared groundwork or premature/speculative scope expansion that should have waited for the tickets that actually need those fields.
- Whether "Decision 4 reversed" (building real PDP wiring in this PR after all) is adequately justified given SFCC-195's own explicit original scope note, and whether the justification given (Figma walkthrough of node 40000307:14062/40000307:13995) is a reasonable basis for reversing a documented scope decision, or whether that reversal should have gone back to the ticket reporter (Jasmijn Tsang) / PO for a real sign-off first rather than being a developer's own call.
- Whether anything from either ticket's AC list is NOT delivered (under-scope) — cross-check SFCC-736's 16 ACs and SFCC-195's ACs one by one against what's actually implemented.

Also flag, for the reviewer's own separate write-up (not yours to resolve): the CodeRabbit thread on this PR raised `.docs/prd/checkout.md`'s CFD-043 (a real-time NewStore/MuleSoft call requirement for Find in Boutique) against the "Coming Soon" placeholder this PR ships for Find in Boutique — confirmed by the author as a real gap, deliberately deferred rather than fixed. Note whether you think this deferral is reasonable scope discipline or should have blocked this PR.

Return a clear verdict per item (in-scope-for-X / out-of-scope-flag-to-Y / legitimate-shared-infra) with your reasoning, plus a final overall verdict: does this PR deliver its two tickets, neither under nor over, or not.

1	# Drawer + Tabs (SFCC-195, SFCC-736) — plan
2	
3	_Built incrementally with Tim, walking real Figma frames and Jira tickets, in `feature/sfcc-52-global-header`'s session on 2026-08-26/27. Saved here per the SFCC-52 precedent (`.docs/temp/SFCC-52-global-header-plan.md`) for review before any component code is written._
4	
5	## Context
6	
7	Building a reusable slide-out Drawer (right-anchored) and a reusable Tabs component for
8	Zimmermann PWA. Immediate scope is two stories:
9	
10	- **SFCC-736 "pdp/drawer"** (assigned to Tim, Squad-A, In Progress) — the drawer _shell_ only:
11	  slide-in panel, backdrop overlay, close button, tab navigation header. Accepts tab content as
12	  children. Does not own tab content.
13	- **SFCC-195 "PDP – Slide Out - Details & Care"** — first tab's content (Details & Care),
14	  triggered by info links on PDP. Depends on SFCC-736's shell/tab API.
15	
16	Known future consumers of the same Drawer/Tabs primitives (NOT in scope now, but the API must
17	stay generic enough for them): SFCC-102 (Size & Fit tab), SFCC-266 (EU Environmental Qualities
18	tab), SFCC-267 (Shipping & Returns + Assistance tabs), SFCC-101 (Measmerize/Find My Size CTA),
19	SFCC-742 (Wishlist login panel — renders as children inside pdp/drawer), SFCC-801 (global
20	country/currency selector — separate right-anchored drawer, same shape), **SFCC-297 (Find in
21	Boutique — confirmed by Tim to use this same Drawer)**. A story also exists for the Add to Cart /
22	View Cart mini-cart (not yet shared/ticketed here) — confirmed by Tim it will invoke this Drawer
23	to display the mini-cart once picked up, consistent with `cart.md` PRD's "opens as an overlay on
24	Add to Bag CTA or bag icon click."
25	
26	## Research findings
27	
28	- **No existing Tabs component anywhere** — not in `overrides/`, not in the base
29	  `@salesforce/retail-react-app` template (confirmed via full grep, zero `Tabs`/`TabList` usage
30	  and no theme recipe). Genuinely greenfield, no in-repo prior art.
31	- **`ZimmModal` + `useZimmModal`** (`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmModal/`,
32	  `overrides/app/hooks/useZimmModal.ts`) exist today but are fully hand-rolled — NOT built on
33	  Chakra's `Modal`/`Drawer` primitives. Centered/fixed-width only, no `placement` concept. Single
34	  consumer: `ZimmSubscribeModal` (newsletter capture, footer). Not Tier 2 yet (only 1 consumer).
35	  **Decision (updated): refactor in place onto Chakra's `Modal` primitive** — see Decisions made.
36	- **Add to Cart is NOT greenfield at the data layer.** `useShopperBasketsMutationHelper().
37	addItemToNewOrExistingBasket(productItems)` (from `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`) + existing
38	  `useCurrentBasket()` (inherited unmodified, Tier 1) already handle the full add-to-basket flow.
39	  A fully-wired confirmation UI already exists too: `AddToCartModal` +
40	  `AddToCartModalProvider`/`useAddToCartModalContext()` (base
41	  `app/hooks/use-add-to-cart-modal.js`), mounted at app root, built on Chakra `Modal` (not
42	  Drawer). No mini-cart/cart-drawer exists in the base app yet. **Tim confirmed a story already
43	  exists** for this (not yet shared) — when picked up, it will invoke our new Drawer to display
44	  the mini-cart. The correct approach is shadowing `use-add-to-cart-modal.js` and swapping its
45	  Modal primitives for our Drawer, reusing the existing context/hook plumbing and data layer
46	  as-is — not building new cart data logic.
47	- **`protectedFiles.md`'s Tier 2 "Shared Hooks" list is NOT aspirational** (correcting an earlier
48	  wrong read) — all 8 named hooks (`use-auth-modal`, `use-toast`, `use-modal-state`,
49	  `use-intersection-observer`, `use-currency`, `use-dnt-notification`, `use-app-origin`,
50	  `use-selected-store`) exist fully-built in the base template today, several genuinely
51	  5+-consumer, none stubs. They just aren't overridden in `overrides/` yet. Tier 2 protection
52	  applies the moment one is overridden.
53	  - **`use-modal-state.js`** (base): `useModalState({closeOnRouteChange, resetDataOnClose}) =>
54	{isOpen, data, onOpen(data), onClose()}`, auto-closes on route change. Currently 3 consumers
55	    in base (bonus-product-selection-modal subsystem).
56	  - **`use-auth-modal.js`** (base): `AuthModal` component + `useAuthModal(initialView)` — full
57	    login/register/reset/passwordless modal system, already reused 3x (`_app`,
58	    `with-registration` gate wrapper, checkout contact-info). Directly relevant to SFCC-742
59	    (wishlist login panel) — the `with-registration` wrapper is a reusable gate-the-action
60	    pattern, not something to build fresh.
61	- **Base `drawer-menu`** (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/drawer-menu/
62	drawer-menu.jsx`, inherited unmodified in this repo) is a real, working Chakra `Drawer`
63	  implementation: `Drawer`/`DrawerOverlay`/`DrawerContent`/`DrawerHeader`/`DrawerBody`/
64	  `DrawerFooter`/`DrawerCloseButton`, `placement="left"`, responsive `size` via
65	  `useBreakpointValue`, multi-part theme styling via `useMultiStyleConfig('DrawerMenu')`
66	  (project theme file `theme/components/project/drawer-menu.js`), focus-trap/scroll-lock
67	  inherited for free from Chakra (not hand-rolled). This is the reference pattern for the new
68	  drawer.
69	- **PRD vocabulary is deliberate**: `pdp.md` distinguishes "slide-out/flyout" from "modal" in 3
70	  places (Find in Boutique, Size Guide). `checkout.md` contradicted this once (calls Find in
71	  Boutique a "modal") — **fixed**: `checkout.md`'s CFD-043 line now says "Find in Boutique
72	  drawer," consistent with `pdp.md` and with Find in Boutique (SFCC-297) confirmed as a Drawer
73	  consumer. `homepage.md`'s "Join Us" capture (already built as `ZimmSubscribeModal`) is a
74	  genuine confirmed centered Modal — so both patterns are real and intentionally distinct in
75	  this codebase.
76	
77	## Decisions made
78	
79	1. **New Drawer built on Chakra's native `Drawer` primitive**, following the `drawer-menu`
80	   precedent — inherits focus-trap/scroll-lock/ESC handling from Chakra for free. Styled
81	   entirely via a new Zimmermann project theme recipe (co-located `.css.ts` per
82	   `overrideStyling.md`'s pattern), not inline props.
83	2. **The "generic hook for other developers" is an override of base's `use-modal-state.js`**
84	   (`overrides/app/hooks/use-modal-state.ts`), not a new custom hook — this becomes Tier 2
85	   protected the moment it's created, per `protectedFiles.md`.
86	3. **One Modal system, not two — `ZimmModal`/`useZimmModal` refactored in place onto Chakra's
87	   `Modal` primitive** (updated from an earlier "leave it untouched, two architectures coexist"
88	   draft — Tim doesn't want two different dialog implementations in the codebase). Same
89	   component name, same public props (`isOpen`, `mounted`, `onClose`, `maxWidth`, `labelledBy`,
90	   `describedBy`, `children`) and same hook name/shape as far as the one existing consumer
91	   (`ZimmSubscribeModal`) needs — only the internals swap from the hand-rolled
92	   portal/focus-trap/scroll-lock to Chakra's `Modal`/`ModalOverlay`/`ModalContent`. Verify
93	   `ZimmSubscribeModal`'s existing story/tests still pass unchanged after the refactor — that's
94	   the acceptance bar, not a rewrite of its own code. In scope for the
95	   `feature/sfcc-736-pdp-drawer-tabs` worktree (foundational dialog work, not tied to PDP), done
96	   alongside/before building the new `Drawer`.
97	4. **SFCC-195 scope is component-only for this pass.** Its AC requires "click a PDP info link →
98	   drawer opens," but `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/` doesn't exist yet at all (fully
99	   inherited from base SFCC) — wiring a real trigger means copy-first-ing a large base file tree
100	   (`product-detail/index.jsx`, `product-view/index.jsx`, dependents), a separate, much larger
101	   initiative. **Decision: build the Details & Care tab content component + Storybook
102	   demonstration of open/close only. Do not touch the PDP page in this pass** — real PDP wiring
103	   is deferred/flagged as follow-up work, not silently dropped.
104	
105	## Figma walkthrough — findings
106	
107	### Drawer Page / Large (node `40002218:42893`, `pdp/drawer/large`)
108	
109	- Frame 1440×1024. `Background Overlay` is a full-canvas backdrop rect (1440×1024) — the
110	  perceived "grey only on the left" is the drawer panel instance sitting on top of it, not the
111	  overlay itself being partial-width.
112	- Drawer panel instance (`pdp/drawer`, x=720, width=720) = **exactly 720/1440 = 50%**, confirming
113	  **Large = 50% of screen** precisely.
114	- Panel instance splits into `pdp/drawer/header` (720×120) and `pdp/drawer/content` (720×750).
115	
116	### Header structure (`pdp/drawer/header` → `drawer/header`, 592×24, inset 64px/48px inside the
117	
118	120px-tall header container)
119	
120	- **`Menu`** — row of `drawer/nav-item` instances: Details & Care, Size Guide, Find My Size,
121	  Shipping & Returns, Assistance (visible) + a **6th nav-item present but `hidden`** — almost
122	  certainly the EU Environmental Qualities tab (SFCC-266), confirming the design already treats
123	  it as a conditional 6th slot, matching its AC ("must only render when `environmentalNotes` is
124	  populated, no empty state"). Item gap = 24px.
125	  - Also 2 `Overflow`-named elements in the same Menu frame, both `hidden` — **no real overflow
126	    visual exists in Figma yet** (confirmed with user). Behavior instead confirmed verbally:
127	    **chevrons render only when the next nav item doesn't fit in the available header width**
128	    (a width-measurement/overflow-detection problem, not a fixed tab-count threshold — matters
129	    because tab labels come from Contentful and vary in length). No design reference for the
130	    interaction once shown (scroll-one-at-a-time vs. partial-reveal-to-hint, etc.) — open item.
131	- **`Navigation icon group`** (separate from Menu, trailing) — `Chevron group` (left+right
132	  chevron, 4px apart) then `Close`. Confirms chevrons + close are a fixed trailing slot, chevron
133	  visibility conditional per above, close always visible.
134	- **Naming note**: Figma tab label reads "SIZE GUIDE" where Jira AC says "Size & Fit" — user
135	  confirmed this is fine since **all tab labels/content come from Contentful** and are editable;
136	  content model design needed (see Open Items) rather than hardcoded label constants.
137	
138	### zimm-\* token mapping for observed measurements (source: `zimmTokens.ts` + `spacing.ts` +
139	
140	`sizes.ts`)
141	
142	| Figma measurement                     | Token                                                                      |
143	| ------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
144	| Header 64px horizontal inset          | `var(--zimm-scale-4xl)` (spacing.4xl = 4rem = 64px)                        |
145	| Header 48px vertical inset            | `var(--zimm-scale-1200)` (numeric alias, 48px — no named-scale equivalent) |
146	| 24px gap between nav items            | `var(--zimm-scale-xl)` (spacing.xl = 1.5rem = 24px)                        |
147	| 16px chevron/close icon size          | `var(--zimm-icon-size-md)` (iconSizes.md = 16px)                           |

152	(`spacing.xl`, `'xl'`), even though both resolve to the same value.

154	### Drawer Page / Small (node `40002218:42900`, `pdp/drawer/small`)

## Per-item verdicts

### Core deliverable — ZimmDrawer / ZimmTabs / ZimmPdpDrawer / DetailsAndCareContent / PdpFooterLinks
**in-scope-for-SFCC-736** (shell) / **in-scope-for-SFCC-195** (content + trigger).

- `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmDrawer/index.tsx` — generic Chakra-`Drawer`-based shell, header-agnostic (children slot), Large/Small/Mobile via `zimmDrawer.css.ts`'s media-query variants — matches SFCC-736's "shell only, doesn't own tab content" framing exactly.

- Independent scroll (AC 10): confirmed structurally — `zimmDrawer.css.ts`'s `content` part is `overflow:'hidden'` while `zimmPdpDrawer.css.ts`'s `content` part is `overflowY:'auto'` — header fixed, content scrolls.
- `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/partials/detailsAndCareContent.tsx` — SFCC-195's actual tab content, presentational, sources `displayName`/`longDescription`/`careInstructions`/`styleCode` — matches AC 4's three merge fields plus the pre-existing style code. `Material` is explicitly and visibly omitted (not silently dropped) with a comment citing the missing SFCC attribute — a disclosed partial gap, not an AC failure, since AC 4 itself names only three fields.
- One soft gap: no story/test asserts backdrop-click-closes (only close-button-click is tested, at `zimmDrawer/index.stories.tsx`'s `CloseButtonClosesTheDrawer`). Functionally almost certainly fine — `<Drawer isOpen onClose placement="right">` never overrides Chakra's default `closeOnOverlayClick`— but if SFCC-736's AC list has a discrete backdrop-close criterion, it's unverified by any test in this PR, worth a reviewer note.

### Item 1 — ZimmModal/useZimmModal rebuild onto Chakra's `Modal`
**out-of-scope-flag** — should have been its own ticket/PR, not bundled here.

Neither ticket mentions `ZimmModal`. The plan's own research notes (`plan.md` lines 31-35) record it as a pre-existing, working, single-consumer component with no functional dependency from the new Drawer work — a new `ZimmDrawer` built on Chakra's `Drawer` primitive needs nothing from `ZimmModal`. The stated reason is architectural preference ("Tim doesn't want two different dialog implementations"), not a requirement of either ticket. Its cost is real and lands outside this PR's two tickets:
- `overrides/app/hooks/useZimmModal.ts` rewritten, `useZimmModal.test.tsx` **deleted** (133 lines).
- `overrides/app/components/footer/index.stories.tsx` — **Tier 2, Global Shell, "Both Squads" owner** per `protectedFiles.md` — modified solely to update `SubscribeSubmit`/`SubscribeModalOpen` assertions for the new animation timing and the `data-scroll-locked` attribute (Chakra's `react-remove-scroll` replacing the old inline `overflow` style).
- `zimmModal/index.stories.tsx`, `zimmSubscribeModal/index.stories.tsx` similarly touched for the same reason.

This is precisely the "unasked-for refactor drags in files with different owners, different tiers" pattern: it is what pulled a Global-Shell Tier 2 file into a PDP-feature PR. Technically well-executed (public API preserved, `ZimmSubscribeModal` needed zero code changes, tests re-verified), but execution quality doesn't change that it's work neither ticket asked for.

### Item 2 — `use-modal-state.ts`
**legitimate-shared-infra** — directly consumed inside this same PR.

Not speculative: `product-detail/index.tsx` calls `useModalState<string>()` and `useModalState<null>()` (lines ~801-816, ~838-843) to drive the two drawers this PR itself wires up. It's a copy-first TS port of a base hook the app already ships (3 existing base consumers per the plan's research), and `protectedFiles.md`'s Tier 2 "Shared Hooks" list already pre-names `use-modal-state.ts` — creating it realizes a slot governance docs already reserved, it doesn't invent new territory. This is the correct minimal-change move, not over-delivery.

### Item 3 — `productInfo.ts` extended `c_*` mapping
**out-of-scope-flag** for SFCC-736/195 specifically, though low-risk and disclosed.

Verified by direct grep: of the 11 new fields (`colour`, `colourId`, `environmentalNotes`, `fabricComposition`, `hsCode`, `sizeFit`, `styleId`, `styleNumber`, `stylingNotes`, `tabDescription`, `tabDetails`), **zero** are consumed anywhere in this diff — not in `detailsAndCareContent.tsx`, not in `pdpFooterLinks.tsx`, not in `product-detail/index.tsx`, not in `product-view/index.tsx`. Only `careInstructions` (SFCC-195's own field) is actually used. `productInfo.test.ts` gained 11 new sentinel-value test rows purely to prove mappings nothing reads. The PR's own comments concede this explicitly (`productInfo.ts:47`: "Mapped but not yet wired into any UI"). This is squarely "premature/speculative scope expansion that should have waited for the tickets that actually need those fields" (SFCC-266 for `environmentalNotes`, SFCC-102 for `sizeFit`, none yet for the rest) — made more visible by the fact the same PR correctly *withheld* `material` for exactly this reason ("Tim confirmed `material = TBD`, no attribute yet") — the discipline to defer-until-needed was available and used elsewhere in this very PR, just not applied consistently to the other 11 fields.

### Item 4 — Real PDP wiring ("Decision 4 reversed")
**in-scope-for-SFCC-195**, with a process caveat.

SFCC-195's own AC (per the brief) already requires "click a PDP info link → drawer opens" — the original Decision 4 deferred this only because `product-detail/` didn't exist as an override yet, a technical blocker, not a scope decision that the AC didn't need it. On the justification question specifically: a live Figma walkthrough (node `40000307:14062`/`40000307:13995`) is a legitimate way to confirm *how* to build something already in scope — it resolved a real structural ambiguity (the 4 rows are trigger-links, not an accordion; Find in Boutique sits outside the tab menu). Reversing a previously-recorded, PR-visible scope decision (Decision 4) was done on the architect's (Tim's) own authority alone, with no visible loop back to the ticket reporter (Jasmijn Tsang) or PO. Given the AC already covered this, the substantive risk is low, but I'd flag to the reviewer that a retroactive confirmation from the reporter/PO — not because the work is wrong, but because a documented scope decision was reversed unilaterally — is reasonable due diligence before merge, not a reason to block on its own.
